_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel just posted its second straight ~20-cent weekly jump — $5.652/gal for the week of 8/24, within 16 cents of the 2022 record, as the Strait of Hormuz standoff keeps diesel futures pinned over $100/barrel. Push the surcharge back up again and don't let a broker point to last week's already-stale number. Underneath, blended spot cooled hard to $3.20/mi all-in, so don't chase soft dry van freight — but reefer's the exception: produce lanes are holding $3.33-3.38/mi, up mid-30s% year-over-year, so hold firm on refrigerated loads even while vans get cheap.

_sourcing.status: TENTH straight cycle with the WebFetch/curl egress block confirmed session-wide (not a freight-site denylist) — see refreshBlockers. WebSearch delivered clean, dated, multi-source confirmation on three fronts this cycle: (1) diesel accelerated further, $5.652/gal for the week ending 2026-08-24, up another 19.8c on top of last cycle's confirmed 19.7c jump — two straight ~20-cent weeks, now within 16c of the June 2022 record ($5.810), driven by the Strait of Hormuz standoff persisting past its expired ceasefire and diesel futures crossing $100/barrel for the first time. (2) Spot finally got a clean, dated, trade-press-sourced reading after nine cycles carried-forward: national blended all-in spot fell to $3.20/mi for the week ending 2026-08-14 (down 2.2% w/w), with per-equipment all-in breakout of dry van $2.93, reefer $3.38 (holding), flatbed $3.54 (down 6-7c) — corroborated across Commercial Carrier Journal and TheTrucker.com, both explicitly citing DAT's seven-day broker-to-carrier all-in methodology for the same week. Promoted spotAllIn from the carried-forward $3.83 (an unrefreshed Q2 2026 snapshot) to $3.20. (3) Reefer cleared the two-way corroboration bar flagged last cycle: $3.38/mi (wk ending 8/14, DAT's own 'Reefer Report: Spot rates slip but hold near the top of the range') and $3.33/mi (as of 8/21, separate search) — two independent dated readings, both above the file's prior $3.11-3.31 range and consistent with last cycle's single-source $3.33 flag. Promoted reefer to $3.33-3.38 with yoy updated to +34-38% (same corroborated report: reefer specifically +35%/$0.68 YoY in mid-August; all three major equipment types +34-38% YoY). Flatbed did NOT need a reprice this cycle — the fresh $3.54 reading (wk ending 8/14) sits comfortably inside the existing $3.46-3.57 range, effectively confirming the old range rather than requiring an upward move; last cycle's $3.65 estimate looks like it was a slightly-stale single-source read. Dry van's own $2.93 all-in data point (same corroborated CCJ/TheTrucker report) sits above the current $2.47-2.80 range but was NOT promoted this cycle — it wasn't in scope of this cycle's flagged reprice review (reefer/flatbed only) and, unlike reefer, only has one dated reading from a single underlying report rather than two independent dated points; flagging as next cycle's candidate if corroborated a second way. Lanes remain carried-forward for a FIFTH straight cycle — no clean absolute $/mi or $/load figure surfaced for either flagged lane this cycle, only percentage moves from DAT's own blog (Atlanta produce lane +9% then +13% over two weeks; Yakima-to-Northeast destinations +10-15% w/w, +9-31% vs last August) and one more evergreen-style lane-guide figure (Miami-Atlanta $2.95/mi 'as of July 6, 2026' from a generic freight-lane-guide site) — same stale-artifact risk pattern flagged repeatedly, not promoted. Commodity rates: Frozen Seafood/Poultry and Fresh Produce nudged from 3.20 to 3.35 in lockstep with the reefer modality promotion (both map directly to reefer $/mi in the app); General Dry Freight, Coiled Steel, High-Value Electronics carried forward unchanged since their underlying modality lines (dry van, flatbed) didn't move.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE, confirmed via WebSearch (primary eia.gov fetch still blocked): $5.652/gal for the week ending 2026-08-24, up 19.8c from the prior confirmed $5.454 (week ending 8/17) — arithmetic checks out (5.454+0.198=5.652). Corroborated across at least five independently-named outlets converging on the identical figure and delta: Logistics Management ('National diesel average sees gains, for the week of August 24, reports EIA'), HaulerMath's live EIA tracker, a Substack freight-surcharge newsletter ('Diesel jumped 39.5 cents in two weeks'), a general-news diesel-inventory piece, and Transport Topics' 2026 DOE regional diesel table. Checked explicitly for a fresher week-ending-8/31 or 9/1 release: EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report schedule shows the week-ending-8/21 data released 8/26 with the next release 9/2 — so $5.652/wk-ending-8/24 is the freshest number that exists as of this refresh (9/1). Driver confirmed consistent with last cycle: Strait of Hormuz ceasefire expiry and re-escalation, now compounding into a second straight ~20-cent week, with diesel futures crossing $100/barrel for the first time (FleetOwner) and the national average sitting only ~16c below the June 2022 all-time record of $5.810.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: LIVE, promoted this cycle after nine cycles carried-forward. $3.20/mi national blended all-in for the week ending 2026-08-14 (down 2.2% w/w), sourced from Commercial Carrier Journal's 'Truckload Spot Rates Drop in Mid-August After Historic Run,' which explicitly states methodology as DAT's seven-day average broker-to-carrier spot rate including linehaul and fuel surcharges. Cross-checked against TheTrucker.com's independent flatbed-specific coverage of the same week's DAT data (same $3.54 flatbed figure), and internally consistent with the per-equipment breakout (dry van $2.93, reefer $3.38, flatbed $3.54 — a volume-weighted blend toward van tonnage lands close to $3.20). Note this reading is dated 8/14, ten days older than the diesel figure driving asOf — flagged for transparency; asOf reflects the freshest verified field (diesel), not spot.
_sourcing.modality: Reefer promoted to LIVE this cycle: $3.33-3.38/mi from two independently dated readings (wk ending 8/14 $3.38 per DAT's own blog headline 'Spot rates slip but hold near the top of the range'; as of 8/21 $3.33 per separate search), clearing the two-way-corroboration bar flagged last cycle. YoY updated to +34-38% from the same corroborated reporting (reefer specifically +35% / +$0.68 YoY mid-August). Flatbed confirmed-in-range via the same CCJ/TheTrucker report ($3.54 for wk ending 8/14) — no numeric change since it already sits inside $3.46-3.57; last cycle's $3.65 single-source estimate looks to have been a slightly stale/high read. Dry van has a clean matching data point too ($2.93 all-in, same report) sitting above the current $2.47-2.80 range, but is carried forward unchanged — out of this cycle's explicit reprice scope and only single-dated so far; flag for next cycle. LTL and Intermodal: no fresh data found this cycle, carried forward unchanged.
_sourcing.commodityRates: Frozen Seafood/Poultry and Fresh Produce moved 3.20→3.35 in lockstep with the reefer modality promotion (both peg directly to reefer $/mi). General Dry Freight (2.47), Coiled Steel (3.57), High-Value Electronics (2.60) carried forward unchanged — their underlying modality lines (dry van, flatbed) didn't move this cycle.
_sourcing.lanes: carried-forward, unchanged, for a FIFTH straight cycle. This cycle's searches surfaced only percentage-based moves from DAT's own blog (Atlanta produce lane +9% then +13% over two weeks, +42% YoY; Yakima-to-Northeast destination cities +10-15% w/w, +9-31% vs last August, per DAT iQ reporting dated 8/26 for prices as of 8/25) — directionally useful but not convertible to a clean absolute $/mi or $/load figure without a known base rate. One more evergreen-style figure surfaced (Miami-Atlanta '$2.95/mile FTL as of July 6, 2026' from a generic lane-guide site) — same stale-artifact pattern flagged repeatedly, not promoted. Still first candidates to reprice if DAT Trendlines itself becomes fetchable.
_sourcing.blurb: rewritten this cycle: led with diesel's second straight ~20-cent jump (now the dominant, cleanest-sourced story, nearing the 2022 record) and the coaching to push the surcharge again; added the newly-live spot-cooling number ($3.20 blended all-in) with the coaching not to chase soft van rates; carried the reefer-holding-firm angle forward since it's now confirmed-live two ways rather than single-source-flagged.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: Lanes (Atlanta-Miami, Yakima-Northeast) and dry van's modality range remain the open items — dry van has a clean single-dated reading ($2.93 all-in) worth checking for a second corroborating source next cycle before promoting; lanes need an absolute $/mi or $/load figure from trade press/DAT proper, not percentage deltas or evergreen lane-guide pages.

refreshBlockers: Re-tested egress first, as instructed. WebFetch to www.eia.gov returned 'EGRESS_BLOCKED' immediately. Raw curl to https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/, https://www.dat.com/, and the https://en.wikipedia.org/ control all returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' (exit code 56), with the agent-proxy logging all three as connect_rejected/organization policy. Also tried WebFetch on several secondary sources this cycle (logisticsmgmt.com, haulermath.com, arktms.com, fred.stlouisfed.org) — all four also returned EGRESS_BLOCKED, confirming the block is broad (not limited to eia.gov/dat.com) and unchanged across all TEN weekly refreshes from 07-07 through 09-01. WebSearch remains the only working channel and delivered strong results this cycle: diesel confirmed accelerating to $5.652/gal (wk ending 8/24) across five+ independent outlets; spotAllIn promoted to LIVE for the first time in nine cycles ($3.20/mi, wk ending 8/14, via Commercial Carrier Journal + TheTrucker.com citing DAT's stated all-in methodology); reefer promoted to LIVE ($3.33-3.38/mi) on two independently dated readings, clearing the corroboration bar flagged last cycle. Flatbed and dry van also had matching fresh data from the same report but flatbed needed no change (already in-range) and dry van was left out of scope for this cycle's explicit reprice review. Lanes still lack a clean absolute-dollar trade-press figure — only percentage deltas from DAT's own blog and one more evergreen-style lane-guide page, not promoted. Broader web-fetch access (not just search) to eia.gov, dat.com/trendlines, or even secondary trade outlets directly would let lanes and dry van get the same clean-primary-source treatment diesel/spot/reefer have now gotten, instead of relying on WebSearch's synthesized summaries.
